applied.problem: "the fault current is measured in milliamps" is absolute, but i3 teaches it grows with system size (a large system passes more); "nothing ties the hull" clashes with the capacitive leak in the next sentence; the half-circle's shape is not set by capacitance, only how far a resistance moves the dot.

Screens 7, 8 and 12 say a first fault passes only milliamps and Screen 12 says "no way home", false after i3; Screen 9 says the curve's shape is set by capacitance, but with equal capacitive leaks it is always the same half-circle (checked: 1 kΩ and 300 Ω figures, peak 463 V near 330 Ω all correct).

"Only milliamps flow" is absolute and fails for a large system after i3; "check a load's line-to-line voltage" invites a live measurement right after the prove-dead safety step, where the board's own meter gives the same reading.

"the curve's shape changes with the capacitance" is false for equal capacitive leaks (the locus is always the half-circle; capacitance only moves the dot along it); the shape changes when the leaks are unequal or partly resistive.
"turns sixty times a second" is stated of all supplies, but only holds at 60 Hz; many supplies run at 50 Hz.
